title: Quentin and the Horizon
premise: Jonah Vasquez has spent fifteen years as caretaker of the abandoned Meridian Seed Vault, hauling cargo through contested orbits and keeping his head down since the Callisto Massacre made him a fugitive from a history that officially never happened. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, a signal hidden in the vault's foundation broadcasts his name to every faction hunting the truth, forcing him out of hiding. Pursued by an Inquisition auditor who believes the official record and a smuggler who once loved him, Jonah must recover the vault's buried black-box archive and prove the massacre occurred before the jump window closes and the evidence is lost forever. He succeeds at terrible cost—exonerating the dead but surrendering his invisibility, choosing at last to belong to something larger than survival.
about_author: Bram Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard Arctic supply vessels before turning to fiction. Their work explores isolation, institutional memory, and the quiet heroism of people who maintain things.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. During a routine cargo run, gravity fails system-wide for exactly nine seconds; in the chaos, the seed vault beneath him emits a pulse bearing his name and a date he recognizes: the day of the Callisto Massacre. Emotional beat: dread—the past knocking on a door he sealed fifteen years ago.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with flashbacks. He inspects the vault and finds the pulse originated from a sealed sublevel not on any schematic—a black-box archive he helped bury after Callisto. Emotional beat: reluctant reckoning as memory collides with the careful emptiness he built his life around.

chapters.title: Auditor
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Sera Okonkwo's POV. She arrives at the vault investigating the gravitational anomaly, carrying official records that show no massacre ever occurred—and a warrant listing Jonah Vasquez as a ghost who shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: cold procedural certainty beginning to crack at small inconsistencies.

chapters.title: Old Frequencies
chapters.summary: Jonah contacts Mara Ilic, a smuggler and former lover who owes him nothing and knows too much. She agrees to help only if he finally tells her what happened on Callisto. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened by betrayal; love offered with conditions.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The trio descends into the vault's flooded sublevels while Inquisition drones breach the surface. Jonah reveals fragments of the massacre: colonists vented to cover a corporate famine-coverup, records rewritten within hours. Emotional beat: grief surfacing like bodies in meltwater.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Cross-checking anomaly data against shipping manifests, she finds nine seconds of erased telemetry—enough to prove tampering, not enough to prove massacre. Ordered to arrest Jonah, she hesitates. Emotional beat: duty straining against dawning doubt.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The archive's core must reach a relay station before the jump window closes in forty hours—but the only ship fast enough belongs to the corporation that wrote the false record. Emotional beat: cornered resolve; the price of the truth made concrete.

chapters.title: Callisto, Again
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A diversionary run turns into ambush; Mara takes a fatal hit buying Jonah time to escape with the core. Dying, she makes him promise to stop running afterward. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved in sacrifice; the cost of survival named aloud.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Jonah and Sera's alternating POV. At the relay, Sera must choose between her orders and the evidence; she opens the channel herself as corporate forces close in. The massacre record goes out system-wide as the jump window seals behind them. Emotional beat: catharsis—the dead given back their names.

chapters.title: The Horizon, Kept
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, epilogue. Months later, the vault becomes a memorial and Jonah its public keeper—visible, accountable, no longer invisible. He plants the first seeds in fifteen years and answers a child's question about Callisto honestly. Emotional beat: belonging earned through loss; survival transformed into stewardship.
